scene.label: Act 5, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. Rome. A Pavilion in Titus's Gardens, with tables, &c.
scene.location: Rome. A Pavilion in Titus's Gardens, with tables, &c.

content.text: Enter Lucius, Marcus and the Goths, with Aaron, prisoner.

lines.text: Uncle Marcus, since 'tis my father's mind
lines.plainText: Uncle Marcus since 'tis my father's mind

lines.text: That I repair to Rome, I am content.
lines.plainText: That I repair to Rome I am content

lines.text: And ours with thine, befall what fortune will.
lines.plainText: And ours with thine befall what fortune will

lines.text: Good uncle, take you in this barbarous Moor,
lines.plainText: Good uncle take you in this barbarous Moor

lines.text: This ravenous tiger, this accursed devil;
lines.plainText: This ravenous tiger this accursed devil

lines.text: Let him receive no sust'nance, fetter him,
lines.plainText: Let him receive no sust'nance fetter him

lines.text: Till he be brought unto the empress' face
lines.plainText: Till he be brought unto the empress' face

lines.text: For testimony of her foul proceedings.
lines.plainText: For testimony of her foul proceedings

lines.text: And see the ambush of our friends be strong;
lines.plainText: And see the ambush of our friends be strong

lines.text: I fear the emperor means no good to us.
lines.plainText: I fear the emperor means no good to us

lines.text: Some devil whisper curses in my ear,
lines.plainText: Some devil whisper curses in my ear

lines.text: And prompt me that my tongue may utter forth
lines.plainText: And prompt me that my tongue may utter forth

lines.text: The venomous malice of my swelling heart!
lines.plainText: The venomous malice of my swelling heart

lines.text: Away, inhuman dog, unhallowed slave!
lines.plainText: Away inhuman dog unhallowed slave

lines.text: Sirs, help our uncle to convey him in.
lines.plainText: Sirs help our uncle to convey him in

content.text: Enter Emperor Saturninus and Empress Tamora with Aemilius, Tribunes and others.

lines.text: What, hath the firmament more suns than one?
lines.plainText: What hath the firmament more suns than one

lines.text: What boots it thee to call thyself a sun?
lines.plainText: What boots it thee to call thyself a sun

lines.text: Rome's emperor, and nephew, break the parle;
lines.plainText: Rome's emperor and nephew break the parle

lines.text: These quarrels must be quietly debated.
lines.plainText: These quarrels must be quietly debated

lines.text: The feast is ready which the careful Titus
lines.plainText: The feast is ready which the careful Titus

lines.text: Hath ordained to an honourable end,
lines.plainText: Hath ordained to an honourable end

lines.text: For peace, for love, for league, and good to Rome.
lines.plainText: For peace for love for league and good to Rome

lines.text: Please you, therefore, draw nigh and take your places.
lines.plainText: Please you therefore draw nigh and take your places

lines.text: Marcus, we will.
lines.plainText: Marcus we will

content.text: Trumpets sounding, enter Titus like a cook, placing the dishes, with Young Lucius and others, and Lavinia with a veil over her face.

lines.text: Welcome, my lord; welcome, dread queen;
lines.plainText: Welcome my lord welcome dread queen

lines.text: Welcome, ye warlike Goths; welcome, Lucius;
lines.plainText: Welcome ye warlike Goths welcome Lucius

lines.text: And welcome all. Although the cheer be poor,
lines.plainText: And welcome all Although the cheer be poor

lines.text: 'Twill fill your stomachs; please you eat of it.
lines.plainText: 'Twill fill your stomachs please you eat of it

lines.text: Why art thou thus attired, Andronicus?
lines.plainText: Why art thou thus attired Andronicus

lines.text: Because I would be sure to have all well
lines.plainText: Because I would be sure to have all well

lines.text: To entertain your highness and your empress.
lines.plainText: To entertain your highness and your empress

lines.text: We are beholden to you, good Andronicus.
lines.plainText: We are beholden to you good Andronicus

lines.text: An if your highness knew my heart, you were.
lines.plainText: An if your highness knew my heart you were

lines.text: My lord the emperor, resolve me this:
lines.plainText: My lord the emperor resolve me this

lines.text: Was it well done of rash Virginius
lines.plainText: Was it well done of rash Virginius

lines.text: To slay his daughter with his own right hand,
lines.plainText: To slay his daughter with his own right hand

lines.text: Because she was enforced, stained, and deflowered?
lines.plainText: Because she was enforced stained and deflowered

lines.text: It was, Andronicus.
lines.plainText: It was Andronicus

lines.text: Your reason, mighty lord?
lines.plainText: Your reason mighty lord

lines.text: Because the girl should not survive her shame,
lines.plainText: Because the girl should not survive her shame

lines.text: And by her presence still renew his sorrows.
lines.plainText: And by her presence still renew his sorrows

lines.text: A reason mighty, strong, and effectual;
lines.plainText: A reason mighty strong and effectual

lines.text: A pattern, precedent, and lively warrant
lines.plainText: A pattern precedent and lively warrant

lines.text: For me, most wretched, to perform the like.
lines.plainText: For me most wretched to perform the like

lines.text: Die, die, Lavinia, and thy shame with thee;
lines.plainText: Die die Lavinia and thy shame with thee

lines.text: And with thy shame thy father's sorrow die!
lines.plainText: And with thy shame thy father's sorrow die

lines.text: What hast thou done, unnatural and unkind?
lines.plainText: What hast thou done unnatural and unkind

lines.text: Killed her for whom my tears have made me blind.
lines.plainText: Killed her for whom my tears have made me blind

lines.text: I am as woeful as Virginius was,
lines.plainText: I am as woeful as Virginius was

lines.text: And have a thousand times more cause than he
lines.plainText: And have a thousand times more cause than he

lines.text: To do this outrage, and it now is done.
lines.plainText: To do this outrage and it now is done

lines.text: What, was she ravished? Tell who did the deed.
lines.plainText: What was she ravished Tell who did the deed

lines.text: Will't please you eat? Will't please your highness feed?
lines.plainText: Will't please you eat Will't please your highness feed

lines.text: Why hast thou slain thine only daughter thus?
lines.plainText: Why hast thou slain thine only daughter thus

lines.text: Not I; 'twas Chiron and Demetrius.
lines.plainText: Not I 'twas Chiron and Demetrius

lines.text: They ravished her, and cut away her tongue;
lines.plainText: They ravished her and cut away her tongue

lines.text: And they, 'twas they, that did her all this wrong.
lines.plainText: And they 'twas they that did her all this wrong

lines.text: Go fetch them hither to us presently.
lines.plainText: Go fetch them hither to us presently

lines.text: Why, there they are, both baked in that pie,
lines.plainText: Why there they are both baked in that pie

lines.text: Whereof their mother daintily hath fed,
lines.plainText: Whereof their mother daintily hath fed

lines.text: Eating the flesh that she herself hath bred.
lines.plainText: Eating the flesh that she herself hath bred

lines.text: 'Tis true, 'tis true; witness my knife's sharp point.
lines.plainText: 'Tis true 'tis true witness my knife's sharp point

lines.text: Die, frantic wretch, for this accursed deed.
lines.plainText: Die frantic wretch for this accursed deed

lines.text: Can the son's eye behold his father bleed?
lines.plainText: Can the son's eye behold his father bleed

content.text: [A great tumult. Lucius, Marcus, and others go aloft to the upper stage.]

lines.text: You sad-faced men, people and sons of Rome,
lines.plainText: You sadfaced men people and sons of Rome

lines.text: By uproar severed, as a flight of fowl
lines.plainText: By uproar severed as a flight of fowl

lines.text: Scattered by winds and high tempestuous gusts,
lines.plainText: Scattered by winds and high tempestuous gusts

lines.text: O, let me teach you how to knit again
lines.plainText: O let me teach you how to knit again

lines.text: This scattered corn into one mutual sheaf,
lines.plainText: This scattered corn into one mutual sheaf

lines.text: These broken limbs again into one body;
lines.plainText: These broken limbs again into one body

lines.text: Lest Rome herself be bane unto herself,
lines.plainText: Lest Rome herself be bane unto herself

lines.text: And she whom mighty kingdoms curtsy to,
lines.plainText: And she whom mighty kingdoms curtsy to

lines.text: Like a forlorn and desperate castaway,
lines.plainText: Like a forlorn and desperate castaway

lines.text: Do shameful execution on herself.
lines.plainText: Do shameful execution on herself

lines.text: But if my frosty signs and chaps of age,
lines.plainText: But if my frosty signs and chaps of age

lines.text: Grave witnesses of true experience,
lines.plainText: Grave witnesses of true experience

lines.text: Cannot induce you to attend my words,
lines.plainText: Cannot induce you to attend my words

lines.text: Speak, Rome's dear friend, [to Lucius] as erst our ancestor,
lines.plainText: Speak Rome's dear friend to Lucius as erst our ancestor

lines.text: When with his solemn tongue he did discourse
lines.plainText: When with his solemn tongue he did discourse

lines.text: To love-sick Dido's sad attending ear
lines.plainText: To lovesick Dido's sad attending ear

lines.text: The story of that baleful burning night
lines.plainText: The story of that baleful burning night

lines.text: When subtle Greeks surprised King Priam's Troy.
lines.plainText: When subtle Greeks surprised King Priam's Troy

lines.text: Tell us what Sinon hath bewitched our ears,
lines.plainText: Tell us what Sinon hath bewitched our ears

lines.text: Or who hath brought the fatal engine in
lines.plainText: Or who hath brought the fatal engine in

lines.text: That gives our Troy, our Rome, the civil wound.
lines.plainText: That gives our Troy our Rome the civil wound

lines.text: My heart is not compact of flint nor steel,
lines.plainText: My heart is not compact of flint nor steel

lines.text: Nor can I utter all our bitter grief,
lines.plainText: Nor can I utter all our bitter grief

lines.text: But floods of tears will drown my oratory
lines.plainText: But floods of tears will drown my oratory

lines.text: And break my utterance, even in the time
lines.plainText: And break my utterance even in the time

lines.text: When it should move you to attend me most,
lines.plainText: When it should move you to attend me most

lines.text: And force you to commiseration.
lines.plainText: And force you to commiseration

lines.text: Here's Rome's young captain, let him tell the tale,
lines.plainText: Here's Rome's young captain let him tell the tale

lines.text: While I stand by and weep to hear him speak.
lines.plainText: While I stand by and weep to hear him speak

lines.text: Then, noble auditory, be it known to you
lines.plainText: Then noble auditory be it known to you

lines.text: That Chiron and the damned Demetrius
lines.plainText: That Chiron and the damned Demetrius

lines.text: Were they that murdered our emperor's brother;
lines.plainText: Were they that murdered our emperor's brother

lines.text: And they it were that ravished our sister.
lines.plainText: And they it were that ravished our sister

lines.text: For their fell faults our brothers were beheaded,
lines.plainText: For their fell faults our brothers were beheaded

lines.text: Our father's tears despised, and basely cozened
lines.plainText: Our father's tears despised and basely cozened

lines.text: Of that true hand that fought Rome's quarrel out
lines.plainText: Of that true hand that fought Rome's quarrel out

lines.text: And sent her enemies unto the grave.
lines.plainText: And sent her enemies unto the grave

lines.text: Lastly, myself unkindly banished,
lines.plainText: Lastly myself unkindly banished

lines.text: The gates shut on me, and turned weeping out,
lines.plainText: The gates shut on me and turned weeping out

lines.text: To beg relief among Rome's enemies;
lines.plainText: To beg relief among Rome's enemies

lines.text: Who drowned their enmity in my true tears,
lines.plainText: Who drowned their enmity in my true tears

lines.text: And oped their arms to embrace me as a friend.
lines.plainText: And oped their arms to embrace me as a friend

lines.text: I am the turned-forth, be it known to you,
lines.plainText: I am the turnedforth be it known to you

lines.text: That have preserved her welfare in my blood
lines.plainText: That have preserved her welfare in my blood

lines.text: And from her bosom took the enemy's point,
lines.plainText: And from her bosom took the enemy's point

lines.text: Sheathing the steel in my advent'rous body.
lines.plainText: Sheathing the steel in my advent'rous body

lines.text: Alas, you know I am no vaunter, I;
lines.plainText: Alas you know I am no vaunter I

lines.text: My scars can witness, dumb although they are,
lines.plainText: My scars can witness dumb although they are

lines.text: That my report is just and full of truth.
lines.plainText: That my report is just and full of truth

lines.text: But soft, methinks I do digress too much,
lines.plainText: But soft methinks I do digress too much

lines.text: Citing my worthless praise. O, pardon me;
lines.plainText: Citing my worthless praise O pardon me

lines.text: For when no friends are by, men praise themselves.
lines.plainText: For when no friends are by men praise themselves

lines.text: Now is my turn to speak. Behold the child.
lines.plainText: Now is my turn to speak Behold the child

lines.text: Of this was Tamora delivered,
lines.plainText: Of this was Tamora delivered

lines.text: The issue of an irreligious Moor,
lines.plainText: The issue of an irreligious Moor

lines.text: Chief architect and plotter of these woes.
lines.plainText: Chief architect and plotter of these woes

lines.text: The villain is alive in Titus' house,
lines.plainText: The villain is alive in Titus' house

lines.text: And as he is to witness, this is true.
lines.plainText: And as he is to witness this is true

lines.text: Now judge what cause had Titus to revenge
lines.plainText: Now judge what cause had Titus to revenge

lines.text: These wrongs unspeakable, past patience,
lines.plainText: These wrongs unspeakable past patience

lines.text: Or more than any living man could bear.
lines.plainText: Or more than any living man could bear

lines.text: Now have you heard the truth. What say you, Romans?
lines.plainText: Now have you heard the truth What say you Romans

lines.text: Have we done aught amiss? Show us wherein,
lines.plainText: Have we done aught amiss Show us wherein

lines.text: And, from the place where you behold us pleading,
lines.plainText: And from the place where you behold us pleading

lines.text: The poor remainder of Andronici
lines.plainText: The poor remainder of Andronici

lines.text: Will, hand in hand, all headlong hurl ourselves,
lines.plainText: Will hand in hand all headlong hurl ourselves

lines.text: And on the ragged stones beat forth our souls,
lines.plainText: And on the ragged stones beat forth our souls

lines.text: And make a mutual closure of our house.
lines.plainText: And make a mutual closure of our house

lines.text: Speak, Romans, speak, and if you say we shall,
lines.plainText: Speak Romans speak and if you say we shall

lines.text: Lo, hand in hand, Lucius and I will fall.
lines.plainText: Lo hand in hand Lucius and I will fall

lines.text: Come, come, thou reverend man of Rome,
lines.plainText: Come come thou reverend man of Rome

lines.text: And bring our emperor gently in thy hand,
lines.plainText: And bring our emperor gently in thy hand

lines.text: Lucius our emperor; for well I know
lines.plainText: Lucius our emperor for well I know

lines.text: The common voice do cry it shall be so.
lines.plainText: The common voice do cry it shall be so

lines.text: Lucius, all hail, Rome's royal emperor!
lines.plainText: Lucius all hail Rome's royal emperor

lines.text: Go, go into old Titus' sorrowful house,
lines.plainText: Go go into old Titus' sorrowful house

lines.text: And hither hale that misbelieving Moor
lines.plainText: And hither hale that misbelieving Moor

lines.text: To be adjudged some direful slaught'ring death,
lines.plainText: To be adjudged some direful slaught'ring death

lines.text: As punishment for his most wicked life.
lines.plainText: As punishment for his most wicked life

content.text: [Exeunt Attendants. Lucius and Marcus come down from the upper stage.]

lines.text: Lucius, all hail, Rome's gracious governor!
lines.plainText: Lucius all hail Rome's gracious governor

lines.text: Thanks, gentle Romans. May I govern so
lines.plainText: Thanks gentle Romans May I govern so

lines.text: To heal Rome's harms and wipe away her woe!
lines.plainText: To heal Rome's harms and wipe away her woe

lines.text: But, gentle people, give me aim awhile,
lines.plainText: But gentle people give me aim awhile

lines.text: For nature puts me to a heavy task.
lines.plainText: For nature puts me to a heavy task

lines.text: Stand all aloof; but, uncle, draw you near
lines.plainText: Stand all aloof but uncle draw you near

lines.text: To shed obsequious tears upon this trunk.
lines.plainText: To shed obsequious tears upon this trunk

lines.text: Tear for tear and loving kiss for kiss
lines.plainText: Tear for tear and loving kiss for kiss

lines.text: Thy brother Marcus tenders on thy lips.
lines.plainText: Thy brother Marcus tenders on thy lips

lines.text: O, were the sum of these that I should pay
lines.plainText: O were the sum of these that I should pay

lines.text: Countless and infinite, yet would I pay them.
lines.plainText: Countless and infinite yet would I pay them

lines.text: Come hither, boy; come, come, and learn of us
lines.plainText: Come hither boy come come and learn of us

lines.text: To melt in showers. Thy grandsire loved thee well.
lines.plainText: To melt in showers Thy grandsire loved thee well

lines.text: Many a time he danced thee on his knee,
lines.plainText: Many a time he danced thee on his knee

lines.text: Sung thee asleep, his loving breast thy pillow;
lines.plainText: Sung thee asleep his loving breast thy pillow

lines.text: Many a story hath he told to thee,
lines.plainText: Many a story hath he told to thee

lines.text: And bid thee bear his pretty tales in mind
lines.plainText: And bid thee bear his pretty tales in mind

lines.text: And talk of them when he was dead and gone.
lines.plainText: And talk of them when he was dead and gone

lines.text: How many thousand times hath these poor lips,
lines.plainText: How many thousand times hath these poor lips

lines.text: When they were living, warmed themselves on thine!
lines.plainText: When they were living warmed themselves on thine

lines.text: O, now, sweet boy, give them their latest kiss.
lines.plainText: O now sweet boy give them their latest kiss

lines.text: Bid him farewell; commit him to the grave.
lines.plainText: Bid him farewell commit him to the grave

lines.text: Do them that kindness, and take leave of them.
lines.plainText: Do them that kindness and take leave of them

lines.text: O grandsire, grandsire, e'en with all my heart
lines.plainText: O grandsire grandsire e'en with all my heart

lines.text: Would I were dead, so you did live again!
lines.plainText: Would I were dead so you did live again

lines.text: O Lord, I cannot speak to him for weeping;
lines.plainText: O Lord I cannot speak to him for weeping

lines.text: My tears will choke me if I ope my mouth.
lines.plainText: My tears will choke me if I ope my mouth

lines.text: You sad Andronici, have done with woes.
lines.plainText: You sad Andronici have done with woes

lines.text: Give sentence on the execrable wretch
lines.plainText: Give sentence on the execrable wretch

lines.text: That hath been breeder of these dire events.
lines.plainText: That hath been breeder of these dire events

lines.text: Set him breast-deep in earth and famish him;
lines.plainText: Set him breastdeep in earth and famish him

lines.text: There let him stand and rave and cry for food.
lines.plainText: There let him stand and rave and cry for food

lines.text: If anyone relieves or pities him,
lines.plainText: If anyone relieves or pities him

lines.text: For the offence he dies. This is our doom.
lines.plainText: For the offence he dies This is our doom

lines.text: Some stay to see him fastened in the earth.
lines.plainText: Some stay to see him fastened in the earth

lines.text: Ah, why should wrath be mute and fury dumb?
lines.plainText: Ah why should wrath be mute and fury dumb

lines.text: I am no baby, I, that with base prayers
lines.plainText: I am no baby I that with base prayers

lines.text: I should repent the evils I have done.
lines.plainText: I should repent the evils I have done

lines.text: Ten thousand worse than ever yet I did
lines.plainText: Ten thousand worse than ever yet I did

lines.text: Would I perform, if I might have my will.
lines.plainText: Would I perform if I might have my will

lines.text: If one good deed in all my life I did,
lines.plainText: If one good deed in all my life I did

lines.text: I do repent it from my very soul.
lines.plainText: I do repent it from my very soul

lines.text: Some loving friends convey the emperor hence,
lines.plainText: Some loving friends convey the emperor hence

lines.text: And give him burial in his father's grave.
lines.plainText: And give him burial in his father's grave

lines.text: My father and Lavinia shall forthwith
lines.plainText: My father and Lavinia shall forthwith

lines.text: Be closed in our household's monument.
lines.plainText: Be closed in our household's monument

lines.text: As for that ravenous tiger, Tamora,
lines.plainText: As for that ravenous tiger Tamora

lines.text: No funeral rite, nor man in mournful weed,
lines.plainText: No funeral rite nor man in mournful weed

lines.text: No mournful bell shall ring her burial;
lines.plainText: No mournful bell shall ring her burial

lines.text: But throw her forth to beasts and birds of prey.
lines.plainText: But throw her forth to beasts and birds of prey

lines.text: Her life was beastly and devoid of pity;
lines.plainText: Her life was beastly and devoid of pity

lines.text: And being dead, let birds on her take pity.
lines.plainText: And being dead let birds on her take pity
